item.title: Ukraine Strikes Crimean Bridge Again—This Time an Entire Road Section Falls Into the Sea
item.summary: Satellite imagery showing damage to the Crimean Bridge following a suspected Ukrainian strike. · Vantor satellite image shows multiple smoke generator ...
item.page_text:
Ukraine has reportedly dealt a major blow to the Crimean Bridge, with part of the crossing collapsing into the water after a second strike in just two days.
Ukraine reportedly struck the Crimean Bridge for the second consecutive day overnight on November 17, with newly released footage suggesting that part of the crossing’s road section and a supporting arch collapsed into the Kerch Strait.
Ukrainian OSINT community Exilenova+ published footage of the latest attack on the bridge, which connects Russian-occupied Crimea with mainland Russia on November 17.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
The strike reportedly targeted an arch near the bridge’s navigable span, causing it and an adjoining section of roadway to fall into the water.
The attack took place overnight between November 16 and 17, following an earlier Ukrainian strike that had already damaged part of the bridge’s structure.
According to Denys Shtilerman, co-owner and Chief Designer of Fire Point, the attack involved Ukrainian-made Flamingo cruise missiles.
Присвячуємо це памʼяті наших друзів і колег Андрія і Юрія без яких це було б неможливо. R.I.P. https://t.co/qYH3HBRvNU
Shtilerman made the claim while commenting on a video published by Anton Herashchenko, which purportedly shows footage captured by a missile-mounted camera during its final approach to the Crimean Bridge.
The footage appears to show the missile approaching the structure moments before impact, although the type of weapon used has not been independently confirmed.
Ahead of the reported strike, Russian-installed authorities in occupied Crimea issued a missile threat warning at 12:56 am, followed by additional alerts at 3:52 am and 5:03 am.
A Ukrainian FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile seconds before striking the Kerch Bridge. Glory to Ukraine! https://t.co/nQceo5A3Rj pic.twitter.com/E7g5ZerzQA
Images and videos circulated after the attack reportedly show significant structural damage, including the collapse of the arch and part of the roadway into the water.
Traffic across the bridge was suspended following the strike, severely disrupting the crossing between Russia and the occupied Crimean Peninsula.
The latest attack came just one day after Ukrainian forces targeted the same bridge on November 16. During that operation, a strike against an arch near the navigable span reportedly caused the structure to tilt, forcing Russian authorities to temporarily suspend vehicle traffic.
Earlier, Ukrainian forces have struck at least six bridges along a major Russian logistics corridor since early October, damaging transport links connecting Russia’s Rostov region with occupied southern Ukraine, including routes used to supply Russian forces in Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, and Crimea.

item.title: Sierra Snow Season Spins Up
item.summary: A widespread, early-season snowstorm blanketed California’s mountains in white in mid-November 2026.
item.page_text:
A widespread, early-season snowstorm blanketed California’s mountains in white in mid-November 2026.
California’s Sierra Nevada got an early taste of wintry weather when one of the first major snowfalls of the water year arrived on November 13, 2026. A moisture-laden storm delivered heavy rains to lower elevations in the Sacramento area and snow accumulations of around a foot to some mountainous areas. The recent bout of wet weather was the first in a quick succession of Pacific storms bringing rain, snow, and wind to the U.S. West in mid-November.
The MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Terra satellite captured this image (right) of fresh snow in the Sierra Nevada on the morning of November 14, during a lull between weather systems. Two days earlier (left), the mountains were mostly bare, with snow appearing only at the highest elevations.
Nearly 12 inches (30 centimeters) of snow fell at Donner Pass, northwest of Lake Tahoe, on November 13, according to the Central Sierra Snow Laboratory . The accumulation snarled traffic on Interstate 80 in the area, prompting officials to close the highway in both directions that evening. To the south, the ski resort at Mammoth Mountain reported 9 to 13 inches (23 to 33 centimeters) of new snow, and officials at Yosemite National Park closed several roads ahead of the storm.
More wet weather and mountain snow are forecast to follow . The National Weather Service (NWS) issued a winter storm warning for portions of the Sierras above 5,000 feet (1,500 meters) in elevation from November 18 to 20. NWS warned of difficult-to-impossible travel conditions, gusty winds, and snow accumulations of around 4 feet (120 centimeters) possible above 8,000 feet (2,400 meters).
NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using MODIS data from NASA EOSDIS LANCE and GIBS/Worldview . Story by Lindsey Doermann.

item.title: The Interactive Shapes of Rivers
item.summary: I'm guessing that many of you will have already seen Dr. Dominic Royé's beautiful visualization of the Shapes of Rivers . His dramatic 'Drop' view of 1,294 of the world's longest rivers has been widely shared on social media this week. But did you know there is now an interactive version of the Shapes of Rivers ? This interactive version lets you rearrange all 1,294 rivers on the fly - switching from the Drop view to a Radial compass burst or a pure geographic Map view without coastlines. You can also equalize river lengths to compare meandering sinuosity side-by-side, group them by continent, and highlight individual rivers to trace their exact geometry. Looking across all six continents in the Map view reveals global hydrology at a glance - essentially mapping landmass geometry using only inland waterways. For example, the vast blank voids across the Sahara, the Arabian Peninsula, the Gobi interior, and the Australian Outback reveal the Earth's great hydrological deserts. Read the original article at Maps Mania . Enjoyed this post? Follow @mapsmania on Bluesky .

item.title: Ctruh launches Verse Engine and streams an entire 10.3-billion-triangle city Into a web ...
item.summary: Ctruh benchmarked the Lyon scene against CesiumJS and Google 3D Tiles, two of the most widely used city-scale 3D platforms, on the same laptop ...
item.page_text: Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India]/ San Francisco [US], November 17: Ctruh , the Bengaluru-based deep-tech company building the infrastructure layer for the spatial internet, today launched Verse Engine by Ctruh , a patented, browser-native 3D streaming engine that turns any 3D environment, however large, into a single link that opens on any screen. To prove it, Ctruh streamed Lyon, a real city in France, built from 10.3 billion unique triangles in a single 556 GB file, straight into Google Chrome on a laptop. Viewers can fly over the whole city and walk down to street level without downloading the file, installing software or owning a high-end workstation. The launch marks a new chapter for the company. Ctruh has incorporated its US entity, Ctruh Inc., has begun operations from San Francisco and is now expanding across the United States. The company is currently raising its Pre-Series A round to accelerate that growth. AI tools, scanners, CAD software and game engines now produce more 3D than ever. Getting that 3D in front of people is still broken. Browser viewers run out of memory at a few tens of millions of triangles, so large scenes are cut down until they lose their detail. City-scale platforms depend on pre-tiled datasets. Cloud-streaming services rent a remote GPU for every viewer, which makes each view expensive and limits how many people can watch at once. Verse Engine takes a different route. It streams only what the viewer can see, at the detail the screen can show. In the Lyon demonstration, just 0.03 to 0.05 percent of the 556 GB file is needed to draw the full city overview. The rest arrives as the viewer moves. Rendering happens on the viewer's own device, so the server GPU cost per view is close to zero, whether ten people open the link or ten million. Ctruh benchmarked the Lyon scene against CesiumJS and Google 3D Tiles, two of the most widely used city-scale 3D platforms, on the same laptop (Apple M5 Pro, Chrome, CDN delivery) on 4 to 5 November 2026: *        11x more detail on screen: Verse Engine drew about 5.9 million triangles in the city overview, against 0.52 million in the tested CesiumJS setup. *        Faster to street level: full street-level detail loaded in about 8.5 seconds, against 11 to 26 seconds for CesiumJS and 13.7 seconds for Google 3D Tiles. *        Quick first picture: the city appeared within 2 to 8 seconds across Ctruh 's test laptops. *        Smooth on consumer hardware: on a Windows laptop with an NVIDIA RTX 5060, Lyon ran at about 45 to 60 frames per second. Verse Engine is the result of more than 3.9 years of research and development in Bengaluru and is backed by 12 patents granted and filed. It is written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly, uses WebGPU where available and falls back to WebGL2 everywhere else. Its core includes virtualized geometry streaming, safe paged memory, GPU feed control, adaptive rendering, and streamed textures and materials. Beyond city scale, the same engine delivers: *         Load times under 2.5 seconds on a mid-tier phone, with about 1 MB downloaded before the first picture appears *         120 frames per second, held for 24 hours straight in endurance testing *         Near-identical colour between phone and desktop (colour difference of ΔE 0.3, below what the human eye can detect) *         Uploads in more than 20 formats, including glTF/GLB, FBX, OBJ, USD/USDZ and IFC/BIM, of up to 2 GB straight from the browser Verse Engine is built for architects and interior designers, real estate developers, construction and manufacturing firms, automotive and product brands, digital-twin teams, game studios and 3D artists. Its Instant Home feature turns a 2D floor plan into a furnished, walkable 3D home in about one minute, which buyers can restyle with a simple text request. It also fits into the tools creators already use: *        One-click publishing from Blender, Unity and Unreal Engine on Mac and Windows, with Substance 3D Painter integration in beta *        REST API and SDK for developers to upload assets, publish experiences, create private links and read analytics *        Website embeds through a simple viewer tag, with integrations for Shopify, Webflow and WordPress *        An early-access MCP server that lets AI assistants upload 3D files and return published links Speaking about the launch, Vinay Agastya, Founder and CEO of Ctruh , said: "The world has spent billions learning how to make 3D, and almost nothing on how to deliver it. Sharing a large 3D world has always meant cutting it down, asking people to install an app, or renting expensive GPUs in the cloud. We refused to accept that. Today we are streaming a real city with 10.3 billion triangles from one file into a browser tab. If a city can open from one link, so can a home, a factory, a car or a game world. Our mission is to make 3D as easy to publish and share as a web page, and Verse Engine is how we get there." With Verse Engine live, Ctruh is taking its technology to the world's largest market for 3D and spatial computing. The company has incorporated its US entity, Ctruh Inc., and started operations from San Francisco, where Vinay Agastya is now based. The US team will work with game studios, AEC and real estate firms, product brands and enterprise innovation teams, and build partnerships across the 3D, AI and graphics ecosystem. The United States is home to the world's biggest game studios, architecture and construction firms, real estate markets, e-commerce brands and enterprise innovation teams, the very people who create the most 3D and struggle most to share it. Ctruh is currently expanding in the US, building its customer, partner and developer base there, with San Francisco as its base for sales, partnerships and developer relations. To power this next phase, Ctruh is currently raising its Pre-Series A round. item.title: Ukraine strikes Crimean bridge for second day as Russia pounds Kyiv bridges | Top News
item.summary: A satellite image shows a bridge over the Kerch Strai. A satellite image shows a bridge over the Kerch Strait, Crimea, November 16, 2026. 2026 ...
item.page_text:
MOSCOW/KYIV, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Ukraine struck the strategic bridge linking southern Russia and Crimea for a second straight day on Tuesday, part of what data suggested was the largest Ukrainian drone attack of the war, while Russia pounded Kyiv's bridges and other infrastructure.
Unverified video and pictures posted on social media appeared to show that the bridge's entire road arch span had collapsed into the Kerch Strait below, blocking navigation. Reuters could not immediately verify the footage.
There was no official confirmation of the extent of damage to the Crimean bridge, a flagship project closely associated with President Vladimir Putin after Russia annexed the peninsula from Ukraine in 2014. The Kremlin said the first attack this week caused only minor damage.
Putin, who is due tomorrow to start a series of meetings in China culminating in a showcase trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping later in the week, has been informed about the attack on the bridge, the Kremlin said.
Sergei Aksyonov, Crimea's Russian-installed governor, said two people were killed in the latest strike and traffic across the bridge was suspended.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy confirmed the attack on the bridge and said it was in response to Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure, including bridges.
"We are ... reminding Russia that war will always return to where it began," he said on X.
In Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Russian forces had struck two bridges spanning the Dnipro River and other infrastructure in the capital.
The 19-km (12-mile) road and rail bridge linking Crimea to Russia's Krasnodar region was once a key supply route for Russian forces in Ukraine. It is now used mainly by residents and visitors, as the military can rely on a land corridor through Russian-controlled territory in southern Ukraine.
The bridge has also served as an important gateway for Russia between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea for ships carrying grain, oil and liquefied petroleum gas, although Black Sea shipping has been severely disrupted as the drone war expanded into its waters.
The bridge has been attacked by Ukraine several times since Putin sent Russian forces into Ukraine in February 2022. A truck bomb in October 2022 killed four people and limited the bridge's capacity for several months.
The overnight attack on Crimea was part of what state news agencies called the largest overnight Ukrainian drone attack on Russia since the start of the full-scale war in 2022.
Russia's Defence Ministry said it shot down 1,441 drones over 22 regions, surpassing the previous record of 1,336 set on Monday.
Air defences repelled a major Ukrainian drone attack on the industrial cities of Ufa and Salavat in Russia's Bashkortostan region, home to several oil refineries, state media reported, citing local officials.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that around 800 Ukrainian drones had flown towards the surrounding Moscow region, 321 of which had been brought down en route to the capital.
The scale and frequency of Ukrainian drone attacks have increased as Russia has intensified its own drone and missile campaign in a grinding war of attrition, with both sides targeting energy infrastructure and other strategic assets.
Attacks have continued despite US-brokered peace talks in Abu Dhabi last week, the first in nine months, and separate meetings between US envoys and Putin and Zelenskiy.
In Kyiv, Reuters witnesses reported a series of loud explosions in the capital overnight.
Klitschko said Russia struck the capital's North and South bridges, a claim later confirmed by Moscow, and partially damaged the metro system. The attacks caused some power and water outages and prompted transport restrictions, he said.
Russia has targeted Kyiv's bridges before, causing widespread disruption.
Overnight strikes on energy infrastructure left consumers without power in eight Ukrainian regions, Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov said.
Outages were reported in Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Sumy, Chernihiv and Chernivtsi regions.
"The situation is extremely difficult in the Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions. Since last week, Russia has been continuously attacking energy facilities in the Dnipro region," Nekrasov said.
In other attacks, local officials on Telegram said three people were injured in the Cherkasy region. They said Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-biggest city, Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia, and other regions were also targeted.
Russia's defence ministry confirmed the strikes, saying on Telegram they had hit transport, military and energy facilities in Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, Cherkasy and Dnipropetrovsk, along with port infrastructure and cargo ships.
Reuters could not immediately independently confirm the reports. Both sides deny deliberately targeting civilians.
Ukraine has sharply increased its strike campaign on Russian oil refineries since the end of October, launching attacks which Zelenskiy said on Sunday had knocked out over half of Russia's refining capacity, something Reuters was not able to independently verify immediately.
Two industry sources told Reuters last week the renewed campaign had reduced Russian refining capacity by about 30%.
Russian officials and media have said the attacks have led to fuel shortages in at least six regions, though without a repeat of the long queues seen at filling stations during the summer.
Kyiv and Moscow agreed on a major exchange of prisoners during last week's talks but there was no significant breakthrough on broader issues, including territory. Russia holds about a fifth of Ukrainian land but the front line in the war has remained largely static for months.
(Reporting by Reuters in Moscow and KyivWritng by Andrew OsbornEditing by Ros Russell)

item.page_text:
By clicking Continue to join or sign in, you agree to LinkedIn’s User Agreement , Privacy Policy , and Cookie Policy .
#30DayMapChallenge | Day 17: Light & Dark
Swiss rock hachures follow the light.
After exploring the big peaks in our backyard this summer, I was inspired to try out Swiss-style rock hachuring. The direction, spacing, and weight of the hachures change with the light angle, creating a shading effect that highlights terrain and steepness. On sunlit faces, strokes are spaced apart and taper toward the ridge, while shaded slopes get denser strokes that taper toward the base. I used slope and aspect to control the direction, width, and spacing of each stroke, then used edge detection to find ridges and gullies. Add some scree, atmospheric perspective, and an easter egg, and it's starting to look like a Swiss map in Alaska.
The map is still a work in progress, but here's a sneak peek!

If you want to fall down the same rabbit hole, these resources helped me:
• Roman Geisthövel's dissertation, Automatic Swiss Style Rock Depiction: https://lnkd.in/gyuu6avv • John Nelson 's tutorial on how to build slope and aspect hachures in #ArcGIS Pro: https://lnkd.in/gJBw872c • The Swiss National Map, the gold standard for rock drawing: https://lnkd.in/gxS-Dn4S • Bradford Washburn's 1960 Denali map, the original inspiration piece: https://lnkd.in/gJjMQGCa #cartogaphy #swisstyle #terrain #chugach
Don't worry, I'm keeping the easter egg knowledge to myself. I will say it was much more challenging to find when viewing the full map 🙂
Nice job! (Another recommended old-school resource: Imhof's Cartographic Relief Presentation.)

item.summary: ... CesiumJS and Google 3D Tiles, two of the most widely used city-scale 3D platforms, on the same laptop (Apple M5 Pro, Chrome, CDN delivery) on 4 to ...
item.page_text:
Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India]/ San Francisco [US], November 17: Ctruh, the Bengaluru-based deep-tech company building the infrastructure layer for the spatial internet, today launched Verse Engine by Ctruh, a patented, browser-native 3D streaming engine that turns any 3D environment, however large, into a single link that opens on any screen.
To prove it, Ctruh streamed Lyon, a real city in France, built from 10.3 billion unique triangles in a single 556 GB file, straight into Google Chrome on a laptop. Viewers can fly over the whole city and walk down to street level without downloading the file, installing software or owning a high-end workstation.
The launch marks a new chapter for the company. Ctruh has incorporated its US entity, Ctruh Inc., has begun operations from San Francisco and is now expanding across the United States. The company is currently raising its Pre-Series A round to accelerate that growth.
AI tools, scanners, CAD software and game engines now produce more 3D than ever. Getting that 3D in front of people is still broken. Browser viewers run out of memory at a few tens of millions of triangles, so large scenes are cut down until they lose their detail.
City-scale platforms depend on pre-tiled datasets. Cloud-streaming services rent a remote GPU for every viewer, which makes each view expensive and limits how many people can watch at once.
Verse Engine takes a different route. It streams only what the viewer can see, at the detail the screen can show. In the Lyon demonstration, just 0.03 to 0.05 percent of the 556 GB file is needed to draw the full city overview. The rest arrives as the viewer moves. Rendering happens on the viewer's own device, so the server GPU cost per view is close to zero, whether ten people open the link or ten million.
Ctruh benchmarked the Lyon scene against CesiumJS and Google 3D Tiles, two of the most widely used city-scale 3D platforms, on the same laptop (Apple M5 Pro, Chrome, CDN delivery) on 4 to 5 November 2026:
*        11x more detail on screen: Verse Engine drew about 5.9 million triangles in the city overview, against 0.52 million in the tested CesiumJS setup.
*        Faster to street level: full street-level detail loaded in about 8.5 seconds, against 11 to 26 seconds for CesiumJS and 13.7 seconds for Google 3D Tiles.
*        Quick first picture: the city appeared within 2 to 8 seconds across Ctruh's test laptops.
*        Smooth on consumer hardware: on a Windows laptop with an NVIDIA RTX 5060, Lyon ran at about 45 to 60 frames per second.
Verse Engine is the result of more than 3.9 years of research and development in Bengaluru and is backed by 12 patents granted and filed. It is written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly, uses WebGPU where available and falls back to WebGL2 everywhere else. Its core includes virtualized geometry streaming, safe paged memory, GPU feed control, adaptive rendering, and streamed textures and materials.
Beyond city scale, the same engine delivers:
*         Load times under 2.5 seconds on a mid-tier phone, with about 1 MB downloaded before the first picture appears
*         120 frames per second, held for 24 hours straight in endurance testing
*         Near-identical colour between phone and desktop (colour difference of E 0.3, below what the human eye can detect)
*         Uploads in more than 20 formats, including glTF/GLB, FBX, OBJ, USD/USDZ and IFC/BIM, of up to 2 GB straight from the browser
Verse Engine is built for architects and interior designers, real estate developers, construction and manufacturing firms, automotive and product brands, digital-twin teams, game studios and 3D artists. Its Instant Home feature turns a 2D floor plan into a furnished, walkable 3D home in about one minute, which buyers can restyle with a simple text request.
It also fits into the tools creators already use:
*        One-click publishing from Blender, Unity and Unreal Engine on Mac and Windows, with Substance 3D Painter integration in beta
*        REST API and SDK for developers to upload assets, publish experiences, create private links and read analytics
*        Website embeds through a simple viewer tag, with integrations for Shopify, Webflow and WordPress
*        An early-access MCP server that lets AI assistants upload 3D files and return published links
Speaking about the launch, Vinay Agastya, Founder and CEO of Ctruh, said: 'The world has spent billions learning how to make 3D, and almost nothing on how to deliver it. Sharing a large 3D world has always meant cutting it down, asking people to install an app, or renting expensive GPUs in the cloud. We refused to accept that. Today we are streaming a real city with 10.3 billion triangles from one file into a browser tab. If a city can open from one link, so can a home, a factory, a car or a game world. Our mission is to make 3D as easy to publish and share as a web page, and Verse Engine is how we get there.'
With Verse Engine live, Ctruh is taking its technology to the world's largest market for 3D and spatial computing. The company has incorporated its US entity, Ctruh Inc., and started operations from San Francisco, where Vinay Agastya is now based. The US team will work with game studios, AEC and real estate firms, product brands and enterprise innovation teams, and build partnerships across the 3D, AI and graphics ecosystem.
The United States is home to the world's biggest game studios, architecture and construction firms, real estate markets, e-commerce brands and enterprise innovation teams, the very people who create the most 3D and struggle most to share it. Ctruh is currently expanding in the US, building its customer, partner and developer base there, with San Francisco as its base for sales, partnerships and developer relations.
